welcome.title: Welcome to Your Creami Kitchen
paragraphs: This book has 50 recipes written for the Ninja CREAMi NC300IN and the Ninja Blast portable blender, using ingredients you can order on Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart, BigBasket or Amazon, or pick up at the kirana. High-protein pints run through the whole book, alongside kulfi-style desi flavours, gelatos and fruit sorbets.

The recipes are split into six sections: Protein Pints: Whey-Powered; Protein Pints: Greek Yogurt, Turbo & Paneer; Desi Ice Creams; Global Classics; Gelato; and Sorbets, Bowls & Shakes. Start with the reference pages that follow. They explain the programs, the sweeteners and the fixes for common texture problems.

Each recipe page shows a program badge (the button to press), a Blast step for blending the base, a 24-hour freeze, the spin and any re-spin. Quantities are metric first, with Indian cups (240 ml) in brackets. Use the notes area to record your freezer's quirks, sweetness changes and the brands you prefer.

how_it_works.text: Add the cold or room-temperature base to the Blast and blend 30–60 s. Cook-and-cool recipes must be fully cool before they go in.
Rest the blended base 2–3 min, or tap the vessel on the counter, so the foam from whey or yogurt subsides.
Pour into a CREAMi pint up to, never above, the MAX FILL line (about 400–450 ml). Lid it and label it with the name and date.
Freeze the pint on a level shelf for a full 24 hours at -13 °C to -22 °C. A slanted pint freezes with an uneven top.
Remove the lid, flatten any hump, lock the pint into the outer bowl and press the program shown on the recipe.
If it looks powdery or crumbly, add 1–2 tbsp milk and press RE-SPIN. Lite and protein bases often need one or two.
Dig a 4 cm well, add up to ⅓ cup mix-ins and run MIX-IN. Flatten leftovers, refreeze, and re-spin before serving again.

blast.intro: The Ninja Blast holds 530 ml with a practical max fill of about 470 ml, so one full pint base blends in a single go. It is cordless and charges by USB-C.
dos: Blend cold or room-temperature bases for 30–60 s, or 2–3 blend cycles.
Add liquids first, then powders (whey, cocoa, gum), then soft solids.
Rest whey and yogurt bases 2–3 min so foam settles before pouring.
Sprinkle xanthan or guar gum over moving liquid to avoid lumps.
Charge it fully before a batch day; one charge covers several pints.
donts: Never blend hot liquids: the sealed vessel builds pressure.
Don't grind hard nuts, ice or whole spices on their own.
Don't knead thick doughs or very dense pastes without liquid.
Don't submerge the motor base in water; rinse only the jar and lid.

golden_rules.title: Freeze a full 24 hours
golden_rules.text: A part-frozen core gives soupy, uneven results. Plan one day ahead.

golden_rules.title: Respect MAX FILL
golden_rules.text: Overfilled pints can jam or damage the machine. Keep bases at about 400–450 ml.

golden_rules.title: Freeze level
golden_rules.text: Set pints on a flat shelf away from the door. A slanted top strains the blade.

golden_rules.title: Flatten the hump
golden_rules.text: If the top freezes domed, rest 5–10 min or scrape it flat with a spoon before spinning.

golden_rules.title: Powdery is normal
golden_rules.text: Lite and protein pints often come out crumbly first. Add 1–2 tbsp milk and re-spin.

golden_rules.title: Never cook whey
golden_rules.text: Heat makes whey grainy and clumpy. Blend it into a cold or cooled base.

golden_rules.title: Keep whey to 1–1.5 scoops
golden_rules.text: 30–45 g per pint is the sweet spot; more turns chalky and icy.

golden_rules.title: Use a pinch of gum
golden_rules.text: ⅛–¼ tsp xanthan or guar makes low-fat bases creamier. Gum-free? Use SMP, inulin or cooked cornflour.

golden_rules.title: Cool before you Blast
golden_rules.text: Cooked bases for gelato, kulfi or chai must reach room temperature before blending.

golden_rules.title: Mix-ins go in last
golden_rules.text: Add them after processing, into a 4 cm well, and use MIX-IN, never the main program.

protein_guide.intro: Protein sources freeze differently. Fat-free and high-protein bases freeze harder, so expect a re-spin and add a pinch of gum. Figures are typical label values; check your pack.

rows.tip: Pair with 15–20 g SMP; gum optional
Thickens on standing; add 2–3 tbsp extra milk
Balance tang with Munkito or fruit

rows.protein: ~12 g / 100 g (~17 g per 140 g tub)
rows.texture: Very thick, fat-free, firm when frozen
rows.tip: Thin with milk; plan one re-spin
Crumble and blend with milk until fully smooth
Use as the liquid; sweetness is already low
15–30 g per pint; over 40 g goes sandy

sweetener_guide.name: Monk fruit drops (Munkito)

sweetener_guide.name: Sugar

sweetener_guide.name: Erythritol / erythritol-monk fruit blends

sweetener_guide.name: Dates
sweetener_guide.tip: Soak in hot water 15 min, cool, then Blast with the milk

troubleshooting.why: Low fat or sugar, or a very cold freezer
troubleshooting.fix: Add 1–2 tbsp milk and RE-SPIN; repeat once if needed

troubleshooting.why: Too much water, too little fat, sugar or solids
troubleshooting.fix: Add SMP, cream or a pinch of gum next time

troubleshooting.why: Too much sugar or honey, or freezer too warm
troubleshooting.fix: Refreeze 1–2 h; reduce sweetener; check freezer is -18 °C

troubleshooting.problem: Allulose pint too soft / melts fast
troubleshooting.why: Allulose depresses the freezing point ~1.9× as much as sugar; too much for the fat level
troubleshooting.fix: Skip the re-spin; refreeze 1–2 h. Next time cut Munkito to 75–80% and add monk fruit drops

troubleshooting.problem: Lite pint powdery even after re-spin
troubleshooting.why: Too few solids or sweetener, or freezer below -20 °C
troubleshooting.fix: Rest 10 min, add 1 tbsp milk, RE-SPIN. Next time add 15–20 g SMP or 5–10 g inulin

troubleshooting.why: Base expanded as it froze; pint not level
troubleshooting.fix: Rest 5–10 min or scrape flat before spinning

troubleshooting.why: Added without a well, or too many
troubleshooting.fix: Dig a 4 cm well to the bottom; max ⅓ cup; use MIX-IN

troubleshooting.why: Whey or yogurt whipped air into the base
troubleshooting.fix: Rest 2–3 min or tap the Blast before pouring

troubleshooting.why: Too much whey, or isolate with no fat
troubleshooting.fix: Stay at 1–1.5 scoops; add 2 tbsp cream or SMP

troubleshooting.problem: Machine won't start / bowl won't lock
troubleshooting.why: Lid, bowl or pint not seated and twisted fully
troubleshooting.fix: Twist the outer bowl until it clicks; check the paddle is fitted

troubleshooting.why: Pint refroze solid after the first spin
troubleshooting.fix: Flatten the top, add 1 tbsp milk, run the program again

troubleshooting.why: Whey heated, or acidic fruit added to hot milk
troubleshooting.fix: Cool bases first; add fruit and whey cold

storage: Flatten the surface of leftovers with a spoon, lid tightly and refreeze; re-spin before serving again.
Plain dairy pints keep best for 2–3 weeks; protein, sugar-free and sorbet pints for 1–2 weeks.
Allulose (Munkito) pints stay soft at -18 °C and scoop straight from the freezer, but melt faster; serve at once.
Refreeze a pint only once or twice; repeated thawing makes it icy.
Label every lid with recipe name, date and program; masking tape and a marker work well.
Keep pints at the back of a level shelf, away from the door, at about -18 °C.
shopping_tips: Keep a standing basket of milk, SMP, cocoa, whey, Munkito and xanthan, so a pint takes one reorder.
Order cream and yogurt last, check the expiry date on delivery, and refrigerate straight away.
Check marshmallows, sprinkles and jelly sweets for the FSSAI green dot; many imported ones contain gelatin.
Buy Munkito from munkito.in or Amazon.in; pick the red Allulose 1:1 pouch, not the erythritol blend.
Buy xanthan, inulin, cocoa nibs, pistachio paste and vanilla extract from Urban Platter on Amazon.
Read the back of 'sugar-free' and flavoured whey packs: INS 955, 965 or maltodextrin rule them out for Diabetic pints.

variants_legend.title: Default, Gym and Diabetic versions
variants_legend.intro: Every recipe in the app comes in three versions. Default is the printed recipe. Gym and Diabetic change only what they need to, keep the base at 400–450 ml, and the "why" note says how the texture holds up. The printed book shows the Default only.

gym.goal: More protein, less fat, minimal sugar, still scoopable.
rules: Per pint: protein ≥ 35 g, fat ≤ 15 g, added sugar ≤ 10 g. If a recipe misses a target, the note says why.
Cream and Milkmaid give way to Amul Sagar SMP, Amul High Protein Milk, whey, skyr or high-protein paneer.
Sweetened with Munkito Monk Sweet + Allulose 1:1; sucralose is an accepted alternative.
Usually LITE ICE CREAM with one re-spin; an optional ⅛ tsp xanthan is fine.

diabetic.goal: No added sugar, less fat, no artificial sweeteners or gums.
rules: Zero added sugar: no sugar, jaggery, honey, condensed milk, syrups, sweetened pulp, biscuits or sweetened chocolate.
No sucralose, aspartame, maltitol or maltodextrin. Munkito allulose or its monk fruit drops only.
Unflavoured whey isolate and plain skyr or curd only; flavoured whey hides sucralose.
No gum in the main method. Switch to "With xanthan" for a smoother pint and fewer re-spins.
Fresh fruit capped at about 100 g a pint; fat roughly half of the Default.

variants_legend.disclaimer: No added sugar is not the same as no carbs: milk lactose and fruit still raise blood sugar. Nutrition figures are estimates from typical Indian label values. Check portions with your doctor, especially if you take insulin or other glucose-lowering medicine.

texture_science.title: Why pints turn out the way they do
texture_science.intro: The CREAMi shaves a frozen block, so texture comes down to how much water freezes and how big the crystals are. Healthier versions change that balance; here is what each part does.

points.h: Why pints go hard, powdery or icy
points.text: Sugar, milk solids and fat keep part of the water unfrozen at -18 °C. Cut them and more water freezes: the pint shaves into powder, or grows large crystals and tastes icy. That is why lite pints often need a re-spin.

Dissolved sugars lower the freezing point. Allulose lowers it about 1.9× as much as sugar at the same weight, so Munkito pints scoop softer. In cream-rich bases use 75–80% of the sugar weight or the pint turns soupy. Sucralose, stevia and monk fruit drops are used in tiny doses and soften nothing.

Skimmed milk powder adds protein and lactose that hold free water and make a pint taste richer. 15–30 g per pint is the useful range; above about 40 g the lactose crystallises and the pint feels sandy.
Fat coats the tongue and breaks up ice crystals, which is why cream reads as smooth. When fat drops, replace its body with skyr, high-protein paneer, SMP or reduced milk, not with more water.
Whey thickens and holds air, but too much binds all the water and tastes chalky, isolate most of all. Stay at 30–45 g per pint, blend it cold, and pair it with SMP, yogurt or a little fat.

Xanthan or guar at ⅛–¼ tsp holds water so crystals stay small. Without gum, use 5–10 g inulin, 8–10 g cornflour cooked into the milk, or milk reduced on the stove as for kulfi. Expect one extra re-spin.
A powdery first spin means the pint is too cold, not ruined. Rest it 5–10 min on the counter, add 1–2 tbsp milk and RE-SPIN. A freezer colder than -20 °C makes every lite pint harder.

label_reading.title: Reading the label
label_reading.intro: Indian labels list additives by INS number. These are the ones that matter for pints and for blood sugar. Check the ingredient list, not just the front of the pack.

rows.what: Sucralose, ~600× sugar. In Sugar Free Natura, most flavoured whey and diet drinks.
rows.verdict: Gym only. No texture benefit; not used in Diabetic versions.

rows.what: Acesulfame-K. Usually paired with sucralose in protein powders and drinks.
Aspartame. In Sugar Free Gold and diet colas; loses sweetness when heated.
rows.verdict: Avoid in cooked bases and Diabetic versions.

rows.what: Maltitol. The sugar alcohol in most 'sugar-free' chocolate and biscuits.
rows.verdict: Avoid: raises blood sugar about half as much as sugar and upsets the stomach.

rows.what: Erythritol. Bulk sweetener in many monk fruit and stevia blends.
rows.verdict: Low impact on blood sugar, but freezes rock hard, recrystallises and tastes cooling. Skip in pints.
Fine at ⅛–¼ tsp. Optional "With xanthan" toggle in Diabetic versions.
Same job and dose as xanthan.

rows.what: Modified starch (hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate). In ready desserts, sauces and flavoured yogurt.
rows.verdict: Fine in small amounts, but a sign of a processed product; cooked cornflour does the same job.

rows.what: Starch-based filler in sweetener sachets, protein powders and 'sugar-free' mixes. No INS number.
rows.verdict: Raises blood sugar as fast as glucose. Not for Diabetic versions.

rows.what: No sugar added in processing; lactose and fruit sugar can still be high.
rows.verdict: Check total sugar and carbs per 100 g.

rows.what: FSSAI allows it at ≤ 0.5 g sugar per 100 g; often met with maltitol or sucralose.
rows.verdict: Read the sweetener list before you trust it.
